item.title: The Fate of the Family and Human Values in Mikhail Sholokhov’s Don Stories
item.description: This article examines the fate of the family and the representation of human values in Mikhail Sholokhov’s Don Stories against the historical background of the Russian Civil War. Using a descriptive-analytical approach, it considers family relationships and the moral conflicts experienced by characters when political and military divisions place members of the same family—and even close relatives—on opposing sides. The analysis suggests that war not only disrupts family structures and social bonds but also creates difficult situations that test individual moral choices. Compassion, sacrifice, forgiveness, and love for others coexist with resentment, fanaticism, violence, and the desire for revenge. From this perspective, the family in Sholokhov’s stories is more than a private social unit: it becomes a narrative space in which the wider crisis of society and the fate of the Don people are represented. Through the consequences of conflict for ordinary human relationships, Sholokhov’s realism exposes the complexity of historical experience and highlights the tension between collective loyalties and personal moral responsibility. The article therefore reads the Don Stories as a multifaceted portrayal of the damage war inflicts on family life and of the endurance—or collapse—of human values under extreme circumstances.
